title: Save Local Business Act
official_title: To clarify the treatment of 2 or more employers as joint employers under the National Labor Relations Act and the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938.
likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Comer (R-KY) with 2 cosponsors. The House adopted a rule (H. Res. 988) to consider the bill, but no passage vote has been recorded. The joint-employer standard is among the most contested issues in labor law; a narrow direct-control test would draw unified opposition from labor and Democratic members, making the 60 votes needed in the Senate difficult.
summary: Narrows when two companies are treated as 'joint employers' under federal labor and wage laws, requiring direct, hands-on control over the workers.
brief: Sets a 'direct, actual, and immediate control' test for joint-employer status under the National Labor Relations Act and the Fair Labor Standards Act.

top_lines.headline: Joint Employer Standard
subs: Joint-employer status requires direct, actual, immediate control
Control over hiring, firing, pay, supervision, scheduling, or discipline
Applies under both the NLRA and the FLSA

items.main: Names the Act the “Save Local Business Act”.
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

items.main: Limits joint-employer status to employers that directly, actually, and immediately exercise significant control over another company's employees.
items.detail: Amends the National Labor Relations Act (Section 2(2), 29 U.S.C. 152(2)) and the Fair Labor Standards Act (Section 3(d), 29 U.S.C. 203(d)). An employer is a joint employer only if each employer directly, actually, and immediately exercises significant control over essential terms and conditions of employment — such as hiring, discharging, setting pay and benefits, day-to-day supervision, assigning schedules or tasks, or discipline. The FLSA applies the same test using that Act's own definitions of 'employee' and 'employer.'

gaps: The bill defines joint-employer status by direct control but does not name how franchise or staffing-agency relationships are treated.
It sets the standard for the NLRA and FLSA only and does not address joint-employer rules under other employment laws.

featured_quotes.name: Mrs. Fischbach
featured_quotes.text: We are here today to debate the rule providing for consideration of H.R. 2262, the Flexibility for Workers Education Act; H.R. 2270, the Empowering Employer Child and Elder Care Solutions Act; H.R. 2312, the Tipped Employee Protection Act; H.R. 4366, the Save Local Business Act, under a closed rule; and H.R. 2988, the Protecting Prudent Investment of Retirement Savings Act, under a structured rule.

modified: Joint-employer test under the NLRA (Section 2(2)) and FLSA (Section 3(d)) limited to employers with direct, actual, and immediate control over essential terms and conditions of employment
